sector: Consumer Cyclical (Auto Tier-1 supplier - climate/comfort seats, BTM, medical patient temperature management)
drawdown_context: Stock at $28 on 2025-05-15, down ~49% from 2021 highs and underperforming the Russell 2000 over 5 years (Performance Graph: $100 base end-2019 to $89.94 end-2024 vs Russell 2000 at $142.93). Underperformance reflects auto cyclical decompression, EV transition uncertainty for ICE-era climate-control content, and Medical segment underdelivery. FY24 still profitable ($65M net income on $1,456M revenue); Q1'25 modest revenue decline (-0.6% YoY) with FX/tax-driven net loss. Forward return +17% confirms re-rating, not distress.

Lear is a direct competitor to Gentherm as part of a vertical integration strategy. OEM breakdown: GM 13%, VW 12%, Hyundai 9%, Ford 9%, BMW 8%, Mercedes-Benz 7%, Global EV manufacturer 5%, Honda 4%, Stellantis 4%, Jaguar/Land Rover 4%, Other (incl. Medical) 25%.

Acknowledging Lear as both #1 customer AND direct vertical-integration competitor is the OPPOSITE of obscuring. Mode B GREEN.

BPS down 22.9% is disclosed in the product-category table but receives no separate narrative — the only 'growth' products called out are Lumbar/Massage (+23%) and Steering Wheel (+10%). Mode B: BPS is the strategic EV product they pitch in Item 1; a 23% decline contradicts the narrative thesis.

The 22.9% decline in Battery Performance Solutions (the BTM/EV thesis pillar) is disclosed in the table but not narratively discussed — a classic 'true but de-emphasized' pattern. rfm_tuples.R: 'The estimated fair value of the Medical reporting unit exceeded its carrying value by approximately 15% as of December 31, 2024. The Medical reporting unit is at risk of failing future impairment tests, as the estimate of fair value does not substantially exceed its carrying value. The Company's estimated future cash flow projections for the Medical reporting unit for the period of 2025 through 2029 assume a compound annual growth rate for revenue of approximately 13.1%, which we deem to be a critical assumption.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: voluntary disclosure of impairment-at-risk language; Mode B: triangulate 13.1% CAGR assumption against actual Medical revenue trajectory ($46.1M FY23 -> $49.8M FY24 = +8.1%; Q1'25 +5.3% YoY). Required 13.1% is ~60% higher than current trajectory. Also: 2023 Medical impairment was $19.5M; $26.8M of Medical goodwill remains.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Critical Accounting Estimates section + EY Critical Audit Matter
rfm_tuples.M_value: Mgmt VOLUNTARILY disclosed (i) the 15% cushion, (ii) the 13.1% required CAGR, (iii) 'at risk of failing future impairment tests' language, AND (iv) EY flagged this as the sole Critical Audit Matter. Actual Medical run-rate: FY24 +8.1%, Q1'25 +5.3% (annualized ~5-8% growth). Gap-to-assumption: 5-6 percentage points of CAGR. This is the strongest 'forward-claim accountability' setup in the filing.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The forecast (13.1% CAGR) is aggressive vs actual run-rate (~8%). HOWEVER mgmt FRONT-LOADED the warning (15% cushion / at-risk / CAM disclosure) which is the OPPOSITE of obscuring. The framework should rate this as honest aggressive forecasting rather than lying. Score MODERATE because the underlying assumption is stretched, not because the disclosure is dishonest. A liar would have said 'substantially exceeds' — they explicitly said it does NOT.

rfm_tuples.R: 'In June 2024, the Board of Directors authorized a stock repurchase program (the 2024 Stock Repurchase Program) ... up to $150.0 million ... During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company repurchased shares ... for $20.0 million in the open market and approximately $60.0 million in an accelerated share repurchase program, and under the 2024 Stock Repurchase Program for $29.9 million and have a remaining repurchase authorization of $120.1 million as of December 31, 2024.' Q4'24 buyback only $10M (Dec only @ $42.84 avg); Q1'25 buyback = $0.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: buyback math; Mode B: capital-action deceleration timing. FY24 first-half $80M ASR+open mkt (March 2024 at ~$45 avg price) -> Q4'24 $10M (Dec only, $42.84 avg) -> Q1'25 $0. Quarterly cadence dropped to zero precisely as the stock fell from $45 to $28 (THE pricing window when buybacks SHOULD accelerate if mgmt thought stock undervalued).
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 5 Issuer Purchases + Q1 2025 10-Q Stock Repurchase Program
rfm_tuples.M_value: Pricing-asymmetric capital allocation: aggressive buybacks ($80M ASR + open mkt) at $40-$45 in H1'24, decelerated to $10M in Q4'24 ($42.84 avg), and ZERO in Q1'25 with stock at $28-$32. $120.1M authorization remains unused as the stock approaches multi-year lows. This is the opposite of conviction — mgmt bought heaviest at higher prices and stopped at lower prices.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B catch: pricing-asymmetric buyback is a leading indicator that mgmt's own confidence is wavering or that liquidity is being preserved for unknowns (tariffs, refinancing, customer downturn). Not dishonest disclosure (the schedule is transparent) but the capital-allocation revealed-preference contradicts the 'we believe stock is undervalued' implicit signal of any active buyback program. The $42M revolver draw in Q1'25 makes this more concerning — they didn't have idle cash.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On February 14, 2024, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration announced that Volkswagen Group of America, Inc. is recalling 261,257 vehicles from model years 2015-2020 to remedy an alleged problem with a suction jet pump seal inside the fuel tank system. ... The suction jet pump is a product originally designed and manufactured by Alfmeier, the business Gentherm acquired in August 2022. ... If the Company is obligated to indemnify VW for the direct and indirect costs associated with the recall, such costs could be material. ... Given the uncertainty ... the Company cannot reasonably estimate the amount and timing of possible costs.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: Note 11 Commitments and Contingencies; Mode B: a 261k-vehicle recall with 'could be material' loss + cannot estimate is a major contingent liability. Test for (i) any update in Q1'25 10-Q, (ii) Alfmeier seller indemnification credit-quality.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K discloses the recall, Gentherm's refusal to accept financial responsibility, intent to provide replacement parts at commercial pricing, insurance coverage carve-outs (manufacturing of replacement parts NOT covered), and seller indemnification under the Alfmeier purchase agreement. No accrual recorded. Q1'25 10-Q: language unchanged (no material developments, no accrual). 14 months elapsed since the Feb 2024 recall with no resolution disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is technically compliant under ASC 450 (loss neither probable nor reasonably estimable), but the 261k-vehicle recall has been unresolved for 14 months with mgmt providing no quantification. Mode B catch: this is the largest single contingent liability in the filing, with the company explicitly stating costs 'could be material', yet no narrative on negotiation status, replacement-part run-rate, or insurance recovery timing. A liar would say 'we expect no material impact'; THRM says 'cannot estimate' which is appropriate but leaves a real tail risk under-quantified.

rfm_tuples.M_value: Strategic narrative (BTM as EV growth thesis) is in direct tension with FY24 operating reality (BPS -22.9%). Carrar (the EV-thermal-management VIE investment) was impaired in 2023 and has only partially recovered to $3.9M carrying. Global EV mfr customer is 5% (growing from 2% in 2022 but still modest). The Battery Performance Solutions decline is consistent with the broader 2024 EV demand cool-down (Ford/GM EV slowdowns, slower-than-expected BEV penetration).

This is the most material narrative-vs-reality gap in the filing. Not a lie because both data points are disclosed, but the narrative emphasis is misleadingly skewed toward 'electrification = growth' when the actual electrification product line is in decline. Honest companies typically address this gap directly in MD&A; THRM does not.

summary: THRM FY24 10-K is a mostly honest cyclical-pressure disclosure with several Mode B flags but no lying signature. Auditor EY (since 2020) is stable with an unqualified opinion and a CAM that ALIGNS with mgmt's own 'Medical reporting unit at risk' language — a hallmark of honest disclosure. Customer concentration (Lear 16% incl. vertical-integration competitor, GM 13%, VW 12%) is granular and named. The cleanest Mode B catches: (1) Battery Performance Solutions revenue DOWN 22.9% directly contradicts the strategic BTM/EV growth narrative without MD&A reconciliation; (2) buyback decelerated from $80M ASR at $45 in H1'24 to $0 in Q1'25 at $28 (pricing-asymmetric — the opposite of conviction); (3) Q1'25 10-Q discloses a $42M revolver draw plus 'customer order forecasts have declined ... significantly for North America' — honest updating but materially worse trajectory than 10-K Feb tone; (4) Medical goodwill cushion only 15% with required 13.1% CAGR vs actual ~5-8% run-rate (front-loaded warning, not a lie); (5) 14-month-old unresolved 261k-vehicle VW recall with 'could be material' loss but no quantification. No going concern, no covenant relief, no auditor change, no restatement, no CFO turnover. Framework verdict: NEUTRAL leaning slightly negative — not a SHORT (too much honest front-loaded disclosure for the lying-detector to fire), not a clean LONG (narrative-vs-reality gaps on EV/BTM and pricing-asymmetric buyback are real Mode B catches). +17% forward return is consistent with honest cyclical-bottom name where the framework correctly does NOT flag distress.
